# Introduction

This article is a brief illustration of how
to use `semeqmodels()`
from the package
[semeqmodels](https://sfcheung.github.io/semeqmodels/)
to find (empirically) equivalent models
of a model fitted by structural
equation modeling using `lavaan`.

# Data

A test dataset of `semeqmodels` will be
used for illustration:


``` r
library(semeqmodels)
packageVersion("semeqmodels")
#> [1] '0.0.0.9027'
head(round(data_test_3_factor_3_item, 2))
#>      x1    x2    x3    m1    m2    m3    y1    y2    y3
#> 1 -2.13 -1.21 -0.05  1.88  0.99  0.40  3.24  2.23  1.44
#> 2 -1.77 -0.91 -0.23 -0.02  0.12 -0.33  0.85 -0.71 -0.72
#> 3 -0.54  0.69 -0.10 -0.33 -0.34  2.31 -1.35 -0.02  0.76
#> 4 -1.72 -1.04  0.07  0.11 -0.13 -0.28 -0.49  1.77  0.64
#> 5 -0.44 -0.41 -0.12 -0.34 -0.27  0.57  2.43 -0.11 -0.20
#> 6  1.42  1.24  0.78  0.47 -0.38  1.72  0.68  1.22 -1.16
```

# Model

Suppose we are going to fit a model
with three latent variables:


``` r
mod <-
"
fx =~ x1 + x2 + x3
fm =~ m1 + m2 + m3
fy =~ y1 + y2 + y3
fm ~ fx
fy ~ fm + fx
"
```


``` r
library(lavaan)
fit <- sem(
  model = mod,
  data = data_test_3_factor_3_item
)
fit
#> lavaan 0.6-21 ended normally after 41 iterations
#> 
#>   Estimator                                         ML
#>   Optimization method                           NLMINB
#>   Number of model parameters                        21
#> 
#>   Number of observations                           200
#> 
#> Model Test User Model:
#>                                                       
#>   Test statistic                                24.970
#>   Degrees of freedom                                24
#>   P-value (Chi-square)                           0.407
```

# Empirically Equivalent Models

Let's defined *empirically* *equivalence*
this way: Two models are empirically equivalent
with respect to a dataset
if the following conditions are met:

- They have the same model degrees of
  freedom.

- They involves the same observed and
  latent variables.

- If fitted to this dataset, they have
  *nearly* the same model $\chi^2$,
  "nearly" defined by a tolerance.

# Illustration

To find a list of models that are empirically
equivalent to the model fitted above,
we can use `eq_models()`:


``` r
mod_eq <- eq_models(
  original_model = fit
)
#> 19 processes started to run model fitting.
#> The expected CPU time is about 0.05 second(s).
```

The output is a list of models, defined
by `lavaan` parameter tables:


``` r
mod_eq
#> 
#> Number of models: 13
#> 
#> The models:
#> 
#>    Model   
#> 1  7cfc96da
#> 2  bc0d3b3c
#> 3  9eefbf8f
#> 4  370609a4
#> 5  31ffe311
#> 6  74f316e6
#> 7  b4893a92
#> 8  fa6f9416
#> 9  1296cb7b
#> 10 834bb36f
#> 11 013c70fe
#> 12 75628bda
#> 13 311a900b 
#> 
#> NOTE: 'default' names are used. Call 'print()' and add 'names_to_use =
#> "long"' to use the long descriptive names, if available, for the
#> models.
```

For more readable printout, call `print()`
and add `names_to_use = "long"`:


``` r
print(mod_eq,
      names_to_use = "long")
#> 
#> Number of models: 13
#> 
#> The models:
#> 
#> Model
#> 1 7cfc96da := original, drop:fy~fm, add:fm~fy, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fm~fx, add:fx~~fm, drop:fm~fy, add:fm~~fy, drop:fx~fy,
#>     add:fx~~fy
#> 2 bc0d3b3c := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fy~fm, add:fm~~fy, drop:fm~~fy, add:fm~fy
#> 3 9eefbf8f := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fy~fm, add:fm~~fy, drop:fm~~fy, add:fy~fm
#> 4 370609a4 := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fy~fm, add:fm~fy, drop:fx~fm, add:fx~~fm
#> 5 31ffe311 := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fy~fm, add:fm~fy, drop:fx~fm, add:fm~fx
#> 6 74f316e6 := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fy~fm, add:fm~fy, drop:fm~fy, add:fm~~fy
#> 7 b4893a92 := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~~fy,
#>     drop:fx~~fy, add:fy~fx
#> 8 fa6f9416 := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fx~fy, add:fx~~fy
#> 9 1296cb7b := original, drop:fy~fm, add:fm~fy, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~~fy,
#>     drop:fx~~fy, add:fy~fx
#> 10 834bb36f := original, drop:fy~fm, add:fm~fy, drop:fy~fx, add:fx~fy,
#>     drop:fx~fy, add:fx~~fy
#> 11 013c70fe := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~~fm, drop:fx~~fm, add:fm~fx
#> 12 75628bda := original, drop:fm~fx, add:fx~fm, drop:fx~fm, add:fx~~fm
#> 13 311a900b := original, drop:fy~fm, add:fm~fy, drop:fm~fy, add:fm~~fy
```

By default, the original model, if
included in this list, will not be
removed.

The function `eq_chisq()` can be used
to retrieve the model $\chi^2$s of
the models:


``` r
eq_chisq(mod_eq)
#> 7cfc96da bc0d3b3c 9eefbf8f 370609a4 31ffe311 74f316e6 b4893a92 fa6f9416 
#> 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 
#> 1296cb7b 834bb36f 013c70fe 75628bda 311a900b 
#> 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025 24.97025
```

The function `eq_df()` can be used to
retrieve the model *df*s:


``` r
eq_df(mod_eq)
#> 7cfc96da bc0d3b3c 9eefbf8f 370609a4 31ffe311 74f316e6 b4893a92 fa6f9416 
#>       24       24       24       24       24       24       24       24 
#> 1296cb7b 834bb36f 013c70fe 75628bda 311a900b 
#>       24       24       24       24       24
```

The function `model_diff_many()` can
be used to list the differences between
the fitted models and each of the
empirically equivalent models:


``` r
model_diff_many(
  target_model = fit,
  other_models = mod_eq
)
#> 
#> -------------
#> 
#> Models: fit vs. 7cfc96da
#> 
#> Model: fit
#> fm~fx (free)
#> fy~fm (free)
```
